title: SagDRE: Sequence-Aware Graph-Based Document-Level Relation Extraction with Adaptive Margin Loss

problem.claim: Document-level relation extraction requires reasoning across sentences and handling multiple relations expressed in the same document.

gap.claim: Existing graph-based document-level relation extraction models do not sufficiently capture the original sequential information from the text.

contributions.claim: SagDRE captures sequential information using sentence-level directional edges and token-level sequential information for encoding shortest paths between entities.
An adaptive margin loss addresses the long-tailed multi-label problem in document-level relation extraction.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on datasets from various domains demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods, according to the authors.

narrative_sequence.summary: Relation extraction is important for natural language processing applications.
Document-level relation extraction is challenging because it requires cross-sentence reasoning and handling multiple relations.
Existing state-of-the-art models use graph structure to connect long-distance correlations.
SagDRE adds sequential information through directional sentence edges, token-level paths, and adaptive margin loss for long-tailed multi-label relations.
The authors report effectiveness on datasets from various domains.

source_observation.claim: The model combines graph-based long-distance connectivity with sentence- and token-level sequential information.

interpretation.claim: Representations for document-level reasoning may benefit from combining relational structure with ordered information flow.

application.claim: For tasks involving cross-sentence dependencies, consider augmenting graph representations with explicit sequence-aware paths or directional edges.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this combination is beneficial outside the reported document-level relation extraction setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or ablation results.
